neighbours.label: text discussing the far right: neo-Nazi, fascist and white-supremacist groups and conspiracy figures (fires on function words inside such passages)
fire: On Sunday, a group of neo-Nazis from a white supremacist gang, the so-called Aryan Front, marched downtown.
Support grew for fascist parties such as the National Front, which openly praised Hitler.
The mayor said that anti-Semitism and white nationalist hatred have no place in this town.
Researchers tracked how neo-Nazi forums recruited teenagers with racist memes.
The rally was organized by a far-right militia that spreads Holocaust denial.
Members of the Ku Klux Klan and other hate groups handed out leaflets near the school.
He became radicalized after listening to conspiracy theorists who call immigrants invaders.
Fascism of the 1930s was built on a myth of racial purity and violent nationalism.
quiet: On Sunday, a group of volunteers from a local garden club marched downtown for the parade.
Support grew for centrist parties such as the Liberal Democrats, which promised tax reform.
The mayor said that rising rents and traffic have become the main issues in this town.
Researchers tracked how gaming forums recruited teenagers with funny memes.
The rally was organized by a teachers' union that wants smaller classes.
Members of the Rotary Club and other civic groups handed out leaflets near the school.
He became interested in politics after listening to podcasts about city budgets.
Politics of the 1930s was shaped by the Great Depression and mass unemployment.

notes: Card: top examples are function words (',', ' and', ' of') inside passages about neo-Nazis, BNP, fascism, Alex Jones; logit effect of the + pole suppresses ' far', ' alt', ' right', ' hate', ' white', ' extremist', ' conspiracy', so the - pole promotes them. The + pole is mainstream US politics (Obama, Bill Clinton, 2008).
